question: Which of the following is NOT among the list of Indian biosphere reserves designated as a "UNESCO World Network Site" in 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve** is located in Assam, India, and is renowned for its rich biodiversity and wetland ecosystems.
 
• It is not part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves as of 2024, unlike other biosphere reserves such as Nilgiri, Panna, and Great Nicobar.
 
• The reserve comprises grasslands, wetlands, and forests, and is a habitat for several endangered species, including the Bengal tiger, river dolphins, and migratory birds.
 
• Dibru-Saikhowa is primarily recognized for its regional importance in conserving flora and fauna but has not yet achieved UNESCO designation.
 
• The reserve is known for its unique ecosystem, including the presence of semi-evergreen forests, deciduous forests, and swamp forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve**

 
 
• Located at the intersection of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is one of India's first biosphere reserves and was designated as part of UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2000.
 
• It hosts a wide variety of flora and fauna, including several endangered species such as the lion-tailed macaque and Nilgiri tahr.
 
• The reserve is part of the Western Ghats, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its ecological significance.
 
 
 
• **Panna Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• Panna Biosphere Reserve is located in Madhya Pradesh and was designated as a UNESCO World Network Site in 2020.
 
• It is famous for its tiger population and is part of the Panna Tiger Reserve, which successfully revived its tiger population after facing near extinction.
 
• The reserve also encompasses diverse ecosystems, including deciduous forests, grasslands, and riverine areas.
 
 
 
• **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• Situated in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve was designated as part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2013.
 
• It is known for its tropical rainforest ecosystems and is home to unique species such as the Nicobar pigeon and saltwater crocodile.
 
• The reserve also includes indigenous communities like the Nicobarese and Shompen tribes, who coexist with the rich biodiversity.
